title: Disagreeing well
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Je ne suis pas sûr que + <subjunctive>

rules.text: THE FORM IS ONE RECIPE: TAKE THE ils STEM AND ADD -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent. ils viennent gives que je vienne, ils disent gives que je dise, ils prennent gives que je prenne. Nothing is memorised verb by verb — you already know the ils form of every verb this course has taught, so you already know its subjunctive.

THE TRIGGER STANDS TO THE LEFT OF que, NEVER INSIDE THE CLAUSE. Doubt, will or necessity in the MAIN clause bends the verb behind que; the subordinate clause itself contains no signal at all. Read leftwards and the mood is decided before you reach the verb, which is what stops a learner hunting for it in the wrong half.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT, OR YOU WILL SUBJUNCTIVE EVERYTHING. il me semble que, je pense que, je crois que and je suis sûr que all take the INDICATIVE: they assert, and an assertion is not a doubt. Only their negative and their question bend the verb — je ne pense pas que ce soit, but je pense que c'est.

SIX FORMS REFUSE THE RECIPE, AND FOUR OF THEM YOU ALREADY OWN. soit, ait, puisse and aille came in as whole words at L3-M3; fasse and sache are the two this module adds. Everything else in the language follows the ils stem, so the irregular list is short enough to hold in one line.

ENGLISH HEDGES BY WEAKENING THE CLAIM; FRENCH HEDGES BY FRAMING IT. kind of, I guess and sort of soften the words themselves. French builds a frame — je ne suis pas sûr que, je ne dirais pas que — and then states the thing plainly inside it, which reads as more confident rather than less.

NOT EVERY HEDGE TOUCHES THE MOOD. ça dépend de takes a noun, pas forcément qualifies a whole clause, and plutôt, disons and franchement colour a sentence without a que in sight. These are the cheapest half of the module and they disagree just as effectively.

THE ne STAYS WRITTEN IN EVERY FRAME HERE. je ne suis pas sûr, je ne dirais pas, je ne pense pas — the negation is what turns an assertion into a doubt, so dropping the ne does not just look casual, it removes the very thing that triggers the mood.

sentences.display: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit vrai
sentences.literal: I not am not sure that this be true

words.display: je ne suis pas sûr que
forms: je ne suis pas sûr que
words.note: The frame, indexed whole: sûr already has its own row at L3-M3. Everything after que bends, because the doubt is here and not there.

sentences.trap: soit is not new — L3-M3 shipped it as a word. What is new is knowing WHY it is there: the doubt on the left of que put it there.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh swee pah SEWR kuh suh swah VREH. sûr has the tight rounded u, and soit is one syllable, swah, with the t silent.

variations.display: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit utile
variations.changed: the claim doubted changes and the frame does not move

variations.display: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit un problème
variations.cue: I'm not sure that's a problem
variations.changed: the doubt lands on a noun phrase instead of an adjective

mistake.display: Je ne suis pas sûr que c'est vrai
mistake.why: c'est is the indicative. The doubt standing in front of que is exactly what bends the verb behind it, so the form is ce soit.

sentences.usage: The most useful disagreement in the language: it doubts the claim and never the person making it.
sentences.mnemonic: The doubt is on the left.

sentences.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il vienne demain
sentences.cue: I'm not sure he's coming tomorrow
sentences.literal: I not am not sure that-he come tomorrow

words.note: The recipe on three regular verbs: ils viennent gives vienne, ils disent gives dise, ils prennent gives prenne. Drop -ent, add -e.

sentences.trap: qu'il is one word and one key — the que has already elided, so the six-word frame of the sentence before it does not appear here.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh swee pah sewr keel vee-EN duh-MAN. vienne has two syllables where vient has one, and that extra syllable is the whole signal.

variations.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il dise oui
variations.cue: I'm not sure he'll say yes
variations.changed: another regular verb through the same recipe

variations.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'elle vienne demain
variations.cue: I'm not sure she's coming tomorrow
variations.changed: the subject changes and the subjunctive form does not

mistake.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il vient demain
mistake.why: vient is the indicative and belongs after je pense que. Behind a doubt the ils stem takes over: viennent minus -ent, plus -e, gives vienne.

sentences.usage: How you decline to vouch for somebody else's plans without calling them unreliable.

sentences.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il fasse froid demain
sentences.cue: I'm not sure it'll be cold tomorrow
sentences.literal: I not am not sure that-it make cold tomorrow

words.note: Two of the six that refuse the recipe. ils font would never give fasse, and ils savent never sache; the other four came in at L3-M3.

sentences.trap: Weather takes faire in French, so it is il fait froid and, behind a doubt, qu'il fasse froid. The verb is the one English would never guess.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh swee pah sewr keel FAHS frwah duh-MAN. fasse rhymes with the first syllable of facile; froid is one syllable, frwah.

variations.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il sache
variations.changed: the second irregular, standing with no clause after it

variations.display: Je ne pense pas qu'il fasse froid demain
variations.cue: I don't think it'll be cold tomorrow
variations.changed: a different doubt frame, and the mood behind it is the same

mistake.display: Je ne suis pas sûr qu'il fait froid demain
mistake.why: fait is the indicative. faire is one of the six irregulars, and its subjunctive is fasse — a form no stem rule would predict.

sentences.usage: Hedging a forecast, which is what French speakers do with weather almost as a reflex.

sentences.display: Il me semble que c'est plus compliqué
sentences.cue: It seems to me it's more complicated
sentences.literal: It to-me seems that it-is more complicated

words.note: The counterweight. It ASSERTS, gently, so the verb behind que stays indicative — the same as je pense que and je crois que.
The participle of compliquer used as an adjective, like annulé at L4-M2. A feminine subject adds an e that nobody hears.

sentences.trap: It seems is a hedge in English, so a learner expects the mood. It is not a doubt in French — it is a soft claim, and a claim takes the indicative.
sentences.sound: eel muh SOM-bluh kuh seh plew kom-plee-KAY. semble ends in a swallowed bluh, and the que that follows leans onto it.

variations.display: Il me semble que c'est trop cher
variations.cue: It seems to me it's too expensive
variations.changed: the assertion changes and the indicative holds

variations.display: Il me semble que c'est plus rapide
variations.cue: It seems to me it's faster
variations.changed: a comparison instead of a judgement, on the same frame

mistake.display: Il me semble que ce soit plus compliqué
mistake.why: il me semble que states something. Only doubt, will or necessity bends the verb, and a soft assertion is none of the three.

sentences.usage: The politest way to introduce your own view — it puts the opinion at arm's length without disowning it.

sentences.display: Je ne dirais pas que ce soit un problème
sentences.cue: I wouldn't say that's a problem
sentences.literal: I not would-say not that this be a problem

words.note: L3-M4's conditional on dire, negated — and the negation is the trigger. Indexed whole, because dirais on its own has no row here.

sentences.trap: The conditional is what makes it polite and the ne … pas is what makes it a doubt. Take either away and the mood behind que goes with it.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh dee-REH pah kuh suh swah un pro-BLEM. dirais and dirait sound the same; only the spelling picks the person.

variations.display: Je ne dirais pas que ce soit utile
variations.changed: the thing declined changes and the frame holds

variations.display: Je ne dirais pas que ce soit compliqué
variations.changed: the disagreement lands on an adjective instead of a noun

mistake.display: Je dirais pas que ce soit un problème
mistake.why: The ne is dropped in fast speech and never on the page. Worse here than elsewhere: the negation is the thing that triggers the mood.

sentences.usage: A refusal dressed as an opinion. It is how you contradict somebody senior to you and keep the room calm.
sentences.mnemonic: No ne, no doubt, no mood.

words.note: A whole answer on its own, and with de plus a noun it becomes a real one. dépendre keeps its de where English keeps on.

sentences.trap: de is not optional. Ça dépend la ville is a sentence with a hole in it, and the hole is where English put on.
sentences.sound: sa day-PON duh la VEEL. dépend ends nasal with no d heard, and the de after it is barely a syllable.

variations.display: Ça dépend de la question
variations.changed: what the answer hangs on becomes abstract

variations.display: Ça dépend de la réunion
variations.changed: the condition becomes an event rather than a place

mistake.why: dépendre takes de and always has. English attaches on and French attaches de; neither language lets you drop it.

sentences.usage: The national answer to a question you do not want to answer, and it is never heard as evasive.

sentences.display: Oui, mais pas forcément ce soir
sentences.literal: Yes, but not necessarily this evening

words.note: The order is fixed. Reversed — forcément pas — it means necessarily not, which is the opposite claim and a much harder one.

sentences.trap: This is the one negative in the module with no ne, because there is no verb for the ne to attach to. Put a verb back and the ne returns.
sentences.sound: wee, meh pah for-say-MON suh SWAHR. forcément carries its stress on the last syllable, and the c is soft.

variations.display: Oui, mais pas forcément demain
variations.changed: the reservation moves to a different day

variations.display: Oui, mais pas forcément ce matin
variations.cue: Yes, but not necessarily this morning
variations.changed: the same reservation on a nearer horizon

mistake.display: Oui, mais forcément pas ce soir
mistake.why: forcément pas says necessarily not — a flat refusal. pas forcément is the hedge, and the order is what separates them.

sentences.usage: Agreement with the timing taken back out of it — a way of saying yes and not now in five words.

sentences.display: Franchement, je ne pense pas que ce soit utile
sentences.cue: Honestly, I don't think that's useful
sentences.literal: Frankly, I not think not that this be useful

words.note: It warns that a real opinion is coming, so it softens the room rather than the claim. Placed first, always, and followed by a comma.
Indexed whole, because pense alone is L1-M9's row. Positive it takes the indicative; negated it becomes a doubt and bends the verb.
One form for both genders. Said of a thing that earns its place, and it is the ordinary word where English might say worth it.

sentences.trap: je pense que and je ne pense pas que are two different frames. The first asserts and takes c'est; the second doubts and takes ce soit.
sentences.sound: fronsh-MON, zhuh nuh pons pah kuh suh swah ew-TEEL. franchement opens nasal and ends on the stressed MON.

variations.display: Franchement, je ne pense pas que ce soit vrai
variations.cue: Honestly, I don't think that's true
variations.changed: the claim doubted changes and the whole frame holds

variations.display: Je ne pense pas que ce soit compliqué
variations.changed: the warning drops and the disagreement stands bare

mistake.display: Franchement, je ne pense pas que c'est utile
mistake.why: Negated, penser triggers the mood. je pense que c'est is right; je ne pense pas que c'est is the one the negation forbids.

sentences.usage: The whole disagreement in one line: a warning, a hedge, and the claim. Rude only if you skip the franchement.
sentences.mnemonic: Negate penser and the mood follows.

sentences.display: C'est plutôt une question de prix
sentences.cue: It's more a question of price
sentences.literal: It-is rather a question of price

words.note: One word, and not L4-M3's plus tôt, which is two words and means earlier. plutôt redirects a claim; plus tôt moves a clock.
une question de is the frame that reframes: it moves the disagreement onto what the argument is really about.

sentences.trap: Disagreeing by reframing rather than by denying. Nothing said before is contradicted — it is simply declared to be about something else.
sentences.sound: seh plew-TOH ewn kes-tee-ON duh PREE. question has the sti of a French t, kes-tee-ON, never the sh English puts there.

variations.display: C'est plutôt une question de temps
variations.cue: It's more a question of time
variations.changed: the real subject of the argument changes

variations.display: C'est plutôt compliqué
variations.changed: plutôt drops to a plain adverb in front of an adjective

mistake.display: C'est plus tôt une question de prix
mistake.why: plus tôt is two words and means earlier — L4-M3's phrase. The one word plutôt is the one that means rather.

sentences.usage: The move that ends an argument by changing what it is about, and it does so without contradicting anybody.
sentences.mnemonic: One word redirects, two words move the clock.

sentences.display: Disons que c'est plus compliqué que ça
sentences.cue: Let's say it's more complicated than that
sentences.literal: Let-us-say that it-is more complicated than that

words.note: The nous form of dire used as an invitation. It proposes a wording rather than doubting one, so the verb behind que stays indicative.

sentences.trap: disons que looks like every other que frame in this module and behaves like none of them. It proposes, it does not doubt, so nothing bends.
sentences.sound: dee-ZON kuh seh plew kom-plee-KAY kuh SA. disons ends nasal; the two ques in the line are both the flat kuh.

variations.display: Disons que c'est plutôt compliqué
variations.changed: the comparison becomes a hedge and the mood stays put

variations.display: Disons que ça dépend
variations.changed: the proposal hands the question back without answering it

mistake.display: Disons que ce soit plus compliqué que ça
mistake.why: disons proposes a form of words; it is not doubt, will or necessity. With no trigger on the left, the verb stays indicative.

sentences.usage: How a French speaker closes a disagreement they intend to keep open — it agrees on a wording, not on the point.
